bib.title: A Succinct Summary of Reinforcement Learning

question: What are the key results of single-agent RL, summarised concisely for readers who already know the field?
contributions: A concise summary of many key results in single-agent RL: MDPs, dynamic programming, model-free prediction and control, policy gradients, model-based methods, POMDPs, and deep RL stabilisers

results.claim: TD(0) bootstraps, adding bias but generally lowering variance relative to Monte-Carlo; n-step returns tend to the unbiased MC return as n grows.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote: Unlike MC methods, TD methods introduce bias into the estimated return

results.claim: MC converges to the minimum mean-square-error fit to observed returns; TD(0) converges to the maximum likelihood Markov model, which can differ.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote:
TD(0) will con-
verge to the solution of the maximum likelihood Markov model which best ﬁts
the data

results.claim: The Bellman expectation backup is a gamma-contraction in the infinity norm, so iterating it converges to the unique fixed point v_pi.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments

results.claim: Every MDP has a deterministic optimal policy, obtained by acting greedily on q*.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote:
there is always a deterministic optimal policy
for any MDP

results.claim: A value function v(s) alone is insufficient for model-free control; an action-value function is needed.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote:
a value function v(s) alone is insuﬃcient
for model-free control

results.claim: Q-learning is off-policy, SARSA is on-policy; the two differ in the bootstrap target (max over next actions versus the sampled next action).
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote:
This learning
is termed oﬀ-policy as the policy used to sample experience is diﬀerent from the
policy being learned

results.claim: Policy gradient theorem; REINFORCE uses the sampled return in place of q_pi and is MC policy gradient.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote:
this leads to the algorithm
known as REINFORCE (Williams, 1992)

results.claim: A state-dependent baseline adds no bias; the value function is the natural choice, giving the advantage A_pi = q_pi - v_pi.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote: If this baseline depends only on the state s, then we ﬁnd it introduces no bias

results.claim: Actor-critic methods update a critic by TD error and the actor by the critic-guided policy gradient, with separate learning rates alpha1 and alpha2.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote: where diﬀerent learning rates α1 and α2 may be used for the actor and the critic

results.claim: Experience replay breaks sample correlation, reducing update variance and overfitting to recent experience; target networks stop a runaway TD target and are synced at intervals or by Polyak averaging.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote:
This breaks the
correlation between samples, reducing the variance of updates and the potential
to overﬁt to recent experience

results.claim: Dyna mixes real and simulated experience; MCTS is MC control on simulated experience and is guaranteed to converge on the optimal search tree.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote:
MC
Tree Search is equivalent to MC control applied to simulated experience

results.claim: In a POMDP the agent can keep a Markovian belief state, but this is intractable for reasonably sized problems, so approximations or learned history-based states are used.
results.source: Sutton and Barto (2018); Silver UCL course
results.setup: Tabular or function-approximated single-agent RL; textbook theory, no experiments
results.quote:
maintaining belief states in
POMDPs will be computationally intractable for any reasonably sized problem

limits: No experiments, no numbers: a reference summary for readers who already know RL (abstract).
Does not cover multi-agent RL, exploration beyond epsilon-greedy, trust-region methods, PPO, TRPO, GAE, or RLHF/LLM applications.
States that deep RL analysis is beyond its scope.
Proofs are mostly sketched or deferred to Silver (2015) and Sutton et al. (2000).
Derived mostly from David Silver's UCL course and Sutton and Barto; secondary, not primary, for those results.
practices: Use gamma < 1 so the discounted return is bounded when rewards are bounded (2.4).
Use a state-dependent baseline, ideally the value function, to cut policy-gradient variance without bias (3.5).
Allow enough exploration during learning, e.g. epsilon-greedy decayed over episodes (3.2).
Use experience replay and a target network (hard copy or Polyak average) to stabilise deep TD learning (6.1, 6.2).

terms.definition: A sampled estimate of the expected discounted future reward, R_t = sum_k gamma^k r_{t+k+1}
The process of estimating v_pi or q_pi
Policies evaluated using directly sampled experience, without a model of transitions or rewards
The policy used to sample experience differs from the policy being learned
A_pi(s,a) = q_pi(s,a) - v_pi(s), from using the value function as baseline
Updates that ignore the gradient of the value function used to define the target
A critic with grad_w q_w = grad_theta log pi, giving no bias in the policy gradient
Distribution over latent environment states, updated from previous belief, action and observation; Markovian
Rollouts all start from the current state, building a search tree rooted there; sample-based rollouts make it tractable
